calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Lightning are one of the league’s best for chance quality, and the Wild are near the top of the league at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Lightning’s chance quality wins out.
calls.call: The Lightning’s chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Wild.
calls.nums: Tampa Bay 5th for chance quality (a 6.7% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Minnesota 6th for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On chance quality, Tampa Bay had 5.9% a shot. The league average is 6.3% a shot, and they came in at 6.7% a shot.

calls.head: Vasilevskiy’s rough record against the Wild is a coincidence
calls.body: Vasilevskiy has been shaky against the Wild since 2023-24, well below his usual. It looks like a pattern, but across three seasons a goalie’s record against one team told us nothing about the next meeting. Expect the usual Vasilevskiy.
calls.call: If Vasilevskiy starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .913 than to his .877 against the Wild.
calls.nums: 6 starts against Minnesota: .877 save percentage · .913 against everyone else
calls.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 6 against Minnesota, 4,587 shots against everyone else
calls.happened: He didn’t start, so this call can’t be judged.

TBL.head: We had this close to even (57% for Tampa Bay), and Tampa Bay came through.

MIN.head: We had this close to even (43% for Minnesota), and it went Tampa Bay’s way.

surprises.head: Tampa Bay hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Tampa Bay’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 48, against their usual 96 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

surprises.head: Minnesota tried a different line
surprises.body: J. Eriksson Ek, K. Kaprizov, M. Boldy played 9:32 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Minnesota’s usual lines.

story.head: The Lightning beat the Wild
paras: Anthony Cirelli opened the scoring early in the first. John Carlson added two goals.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. By our Swing measure, Quinn Hughes had the best night of anyone, even in a loss. The Wild tried a line they hadn’t used before: Joel Eriksson Ek, Kirill Kaprizov and Matt Boldy.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Lightning.
Whether the Wild keep that line together in Florida on Saturday.
